readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckPartialDerivativeBridge.partialLower_eq_joint_derivative
readback.mathematical_statement: E is the fixed real three-dimensional Euclidean space ClosedSmoothModel 3. Bilin is E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R and Jet1 is E ->L[R] Bilin. Background is E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E, BackgroundDerivative is E ->L[R] Background, BackgroundPair is Background times BackgroundDerivative, MetricJet is Bilin times Jet1, and Joint is BackgroundPair times MetricJet. The canonical CLM group/real normed-space bindings in the literal fix real source and target scalars and RingHom.id R for Jet1 and both background map spaces, retaining their existing operator norms and real scalar actions. The explicit Prod.instAddCommMonoid cache on MetricJet is the standard componentwise pair addition and zero, with no supplied hypothesis or replacement algebra. Let B be any Background, DB any BackgroundDerivative, G0 any Bilin, and J0 any Jet1, and assume only G0.IsInvertible as a continuous real-linear map E -> E dual, meaning it is the forward map of a continuous linear equivalence. No symmetry, positive-definiteness, realized metric/jet/background condition, unit/determinant premise, or derivative operator package is assumed. Let p0=((B,DB),(G0,J0)). The pinned jointLower maps ((B,DB),(G,J)) to the actual Bilin-valued DeTurckPrincipalIdentity.lowerTerm B DB G J. The pinned partialLower(p0) is exactly DeTurckJetLinearization.lowerDifferential B DB G0 J0, namely fderiv R at (G0,J0) of the actual map (G,J) |-> lowerTerm B DB G J. The pinned metricInclusion : MetricJet ->L[R] Joint is ContinuousLinearMap.inr R BackgroundPair MetricJet and sends h=(hG,hJ) exactly to ((0_BG,0_DB),h). Then partialLower(p0) equals (fderiv R jointLower p0).comp metricInclusion as whole continuous real-linear maps MetricJet ->L[R] Bilin. Composition first includes the metric/first-jet direction with both background directions zero, then applies the full joint derivative. In particular for every h, the equality means partialLower(p0)(h) = D jointLower(p0)((0,0),h), preserving both hG and hJ while excluding variation of B and DB in this partial derivative. B and DB may be arbitrary independent basepoint data; DB is not assumed to be a realized derivative of a background field. This is an equality of the existing actual partial derivative with the restricted existing joint derivative, rather than construction from a supplied CLM or merely equality of scalar values in selected tensor slots. The same original product and CLM operator-norm structures are used. There are no universe parameters, manifold, chart point, time, Hoelder exponent, second metric jet, spatial coefficient field, quantitative bound, or flow premise. The theorem asserts this bridge at each invertible base metric. It does not itself claim global smoothness at singular forms, spatial coefficient regularity, the principal inverse-variation/second-jet contribution, a bounded global L, covariance, a residual/contraction, or physical flow.
